Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Conversation, family & daily routines

abuse noun

insults, rude words

also verbal abuse, insults, insult, call names, swear at, hurl abuse

classical

Cic. Cael. 6 (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Ad. 2.1.26: convīcium facere

convīcium, convīciī n.

noun, second declension

loud abuse, insults, a scolding

Properly a loud noise, an outcry (of a crowd, of frogs, of cicadas); then, most often, loud abuse. Cicero: an insult thrown petulantius, rudely, is a convīcium (Cael. 6). Convīcium facere alicui, to shout abuse at someone.

Other words

  • maledictum, maledictī n. — an insult, a rude word

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Publil. Syr. M 23

    A word said against someone; the verb is maledīcere with the dative (Cic. Deiot. 28), which Cicero distinguishes from a formal accusation (Cael. 6).

  • male dīcere (+ dative) — to speak ill of, abuse

    phrase, also written as one word, maledīcō, maledīcere, maledīxī, maledictum · also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 1.2.10: quī bonīs dīcunt male (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • saepe manū summā lacrimantia lūmina terget immeritōque furēns dīcit convīcia fūmō

    often he wipes his streaming eyes with the back of his hand, and in a rage swears at the blameless smokeMor. 109–110

  • Maledictum interpretandō faciās ācrius.

    explain an insult and you make it sharperPublil. Syr. M 23

See also abuse, attack, argument.
